spatialPolicy.fence: Circular arc through LF/CF/RF posts at -45/0/+45 degrees, matching the existing RoundFence construction; no linear chevron
spatialPolicy.bags: Trial bag centers scale the audited rounded coordinates by basepath/90; migrate control exactly before considering coordinate precision separately

spatialPolicy.outfieldStarts: Preserve bearing and starting radius/fence-at-bearing fraction; evaluate gap and wall retrieval before accepting final starts
spatialPolicy.bodyAndEquipment: Preserve character stature, equipment, bag size, home/stance/catcher group and wall height for trial comparison

clockComparisonPolicy.runner: Accepted F693-05-runner-clock: retain current stat-to-bag elapsed times, 0.5-second batter startup and explicit dash schedule as C80 calibration anchor. Derive linear speeds from candidate distance. Exact path/rounding/slide arrivals remain to be validated.
clockComparisonPolicy.pursuit: One ordinary profile per character is accepted. Calculate separate IF and OF time-preserving speed sensitivities; neither is a selected coefficient or a feasible joint solution.
clockComparisonPolicy.throw: Accepted ordinary anchors: 0.30-second command-to-release with immediate motion, then 0.90-second flight over 80 ft for a neutral middle arm with proportional infield travel times. Actual eligible reception is separate from target arrival. Long-throw range and pace loss are accepted below; relay command-per-leg direction is accepted, with exact buffer/cancel details pending; no extra .22-second hold. Accepted long-throw direction: moderate smooth arm-dependent loss of pace with direct choice preserved and chemistry included in the direct/relay comparison. Good-pair chemistry is accepted at 1.30x travel speed per actual pair, ordinary release unchanged. Long-range curve is accepted under F693-03-long-throw-numbers. Bad-pair chemistry is accepted at 0.90x travel speed per actual pair, replacing the extra random slant. Special stacking remains pending.
clockComparisonPolicy.read: Brief visible read and responsive acceleration are accepted directions. Numerical values pending; no additional camera-completion gate.
clockComparisonPolicy.flight: Fixed-input and tactical comparisons both required. Carry, hang, bounce, roll, wall interaction and contact-class distinctions need coordinated calibration; no uniform spatial transform can solve the independently scaled field.
clockComparisonPolicy.coverage: Record ball-target arrival, receiver eligibility/possession and runner arrival separately; target arrival is not an out.
clockComparisonPolicy.scoring: Accepted 1.8–5 home and away means separately for each S29 and Harbor cohort; no pooling. Baseline Harbor failures remain open.
clockComparisonPolicy.presentation: D7 unchanged. Dead-ball duration and moderate ball assistance remain pending numerical presentation decisions.

decisionQueue.question: Which spatial trial leads: C80 or C70?
Preserve current runner elapsed pace as the compact comparison anchor, or change it?
Use 0.30 seconds from accepted ordinary throw command in clean possession to release as the trial baseline?
Use 0.90 seconds of ordinary infield flight over 80 feet, proportional to distance, as the trial anchor?
Keep direct throws available, with moderate arm-dependent pace loss at long range so a well-positioned relay can beat a very long direct throw?
Retain the existing 1.30x good-chemistry travel-speed bonus per actual thrower-receiver pair, with no extra chain bonus or shortening of the ordinary release?
Use a 160-foot middle-arm comfortable range, varying 5 feet per Field point, with smooth extra flight time of 0.60 seconds at 80 feet beyond that range, as the trial profile?
Replace bad chemistry’s extra random slant with a predictable 0.90x travel-speed factor per bad pair, leaving ordinary release and other accuracy rules separately governed?
Require a separate player throw command for each relay leg, allowing an early buffered command for the next receiver, with hold and retarget before commitment?
Make Snap Throw a 0.22-second release after cleanly receiving a teammate throw, replacing its 1.22x flight-speed boost?
Review Laser activation and travel-speed effect, including chemistry and long-range stacking.
Choose the early-input window and exact cancel/retarget controls individually, including receiver recovery cases.
Review a common pursuit profile with read, acceleration and coverage against both routine defense and deep-hit races.
Review contact-class flight, bounce/roll and wall-play tradeoffs within the selected space.
Review result pacing and numerical readability aids individually after the sim contract is coherent.

runnerClockProposal.recommendation: Preserve current stat-to-bag elapsed times, batter startup and explicit dash schedule for the C80 calibration anchor; derive ordinary linear speed from the shorter path.
runnerClockProposal.scope: Elapsed calibration anchor, not acceptance of every rounded/slide/reversal path, exact first-base arrival, visual run-cycle cadence, or fielding speed. No compact simulation yet.
runnerClockProposal.referenceLimit: Wii survey reports Pianta third-to-home 3.65 s without a matched stock speed/input/start protocol. GameCube running mechanics include acceleration/dash/stamina; no matched average-runner elapsed target is established. This is a Harbor trial anchor, not measured Mario equivalence.
runnerClockProposal.acceptanceEvidence: Jack replied approve. to preserving approximately 3.45-second ordinary first-base pace for the compact trial, including current stat differences and dash.

throwReleaseProposal.scope: Clean ordinary throw with ball possessed, baseline Field-5 character: accepted throw command starts motion immediately; ball separates at 0.30 s. Human thinking time, pickup/read, recovery, follow-through duration and flight excluded. Stat/ability adjustments and buffering rules not selected by this scalar.
throwReleaseProposal.referenceStatus: Authored Harbor trial, not measured Mario command-to-release. Prior Wii possession-to-release includes unknown player delay; GameCube gather/release bracket has no known command timestamp. Video re-fetch failed this turn; retained #701 annotations used.
throwReleaseProposal.rationale: Allow more visible transfer than the current authored 0.18 s marker while beginning response immediately; assess travel separately. Human visual acceptance remains open.
throwReleaseProposal.raceConstraint: Do not append this duration to all existing delays. Pickup, command policy, release, travel and cover must fit the accepted runner clock; do not slow runners to rescue a failed throw.

arithmeticOnlyExample.status: Feasibility arithmetic only; runner and release anchors accepted; possession, human decision, flight and margin are not accepted targets or simulated results.

throwReleaseProposal.acceptanceEvidence: Jack replied approve to 0.30 seconds as ordinary release timing for the trial, with immediate motion onset and ball travel reviewed separately.

throwTravelProposal.scope: Ordinary infield throw, Field-5 neutral arm without ability/chemistry/lob modifiers; flight from actual release to target arrival, followed by actual eligible reception. Proportional to horizontal distance in this regime. Example distances are not hard regime boundaries. Longer throws/relay range and exact modifiers require the next review.
throwTravelProposal.armPolicy: Preserve meaningful character arm differences; examples use the ordinary neutral arm. No new Field-to-release adjustment or ability change is selected.
throwTravelProposal.sourceStatus: Authored trial timing. #701 Wii release-to-reception observation 0.99–1.21 s has unmatched distance/stats; GC return has wider release/reception uncertainty. No reference feet-per-second measured.

baselineComparison.scope: Neutral middle arm only. Historical .22 intercept was sampled travel; proposed .30 is a distinct held-ball release phase.

raceExample.status: Illustrative arithmetic, not simulation; runner, release and infield travel anchors accepted; possession, human decision and margin remain unapproved examples.

alternatives.effect: More defensive time and a sharper ball, but less time to follow travel.
More deliberate flight, but spends another 0.20 seconds per 80 feet of the defensive race.

throwTravelProposal.relayConstraint: Do not extrapolate the near-field rate as an accepted whole-field curve. Two equal-arm collinear relay legs at one constant speed add a second release and cannot beat a direct throw purely on flight time. Review existing reach/cutoff rules at compact dimensions before selecting the long-range contract.
throwTravelProposal.acceptanceEvidence: Jack replied yes to 0.90 seconds over 80 feet as the ordinary infield travel baseline, with proportional infield travel times and long throws/relays reviewed separately.

longThrowProposal.recommendation: Retain direct throws as a player choice; add moderate smooth arm-dependent long-range pace loss, so a well-positioned relay can sometimes win after its real catch/decision/release cost. Strong arms remain useful for direct throws; short and medium direct throws remain efficient.
longThrowProposal.longRangeTimingCurve: Accepted under F693-03-long-throw-numbers; see longRangeProfileProposal for full arm/range/chemistry formula.
longThrowProposal.scope: Behavior choice only. Range, rate of pace loss, exact arm/ability/chemistry interactions, arc/velocity shape, receiving delays and input buffering remain to be specified. No universal relay advantage or automatic outcome.

currentCodeAudit.scope: Flat distance threshold in CPU route and forecast; it does not multiply range by arm stat. Human BeginPlayerThrowOrCommit has an explicit cutoff branch and otherwise permits direct bag throws. Do not claim every human throw over 200 feet is already forced through a cutoff.

sources.kind: Nintendo primary booklet hosted by mirror

longThrowProposal.referenceLimit: Manuals support the cutoff verb, not the proposed long-throw slowdown mechanism. This is an original Harbor design proposal; matched long-throw measurements for both titles remain outstanding.

breakEvenExample.status: Counterfactual constant-speed arithmetic only; 240-ft extrapolation is not an accepted long-throw curve, relay decision .20 s is not approved, receivers assumed ready with perfect alignment. A beneficial long-throw model must beat actual additional relay time, not invent a free second release.

acceptanceChecks: Direct throw remains selectable; CPU evaluates the same actual model and receiver coverage.
No speed discontinuity at a distance threshold or hidden forced redirection.
A clean deep relay can beat a sufficiently long ordinary direct throw; a poor or unnecessary relay can lose.
Strong and weak arms differ meaningfully; explicit special throws remain separately identified.
The 0.30-second ordinary release occurs on each actual commanded leg; relay continuation control is reviewed separately from this physics decision.
No coefficients enter runtime before the complete contract, shared-geometry parity and full-race validation.

longThrowProposal.chemistryQualification: Chemistry participates in direct-versus-relay calibration; F693-03-good-chemistry subsequently accepts the 1.30x travel-speed treatment per actual pair with ordinary release unchanged. Negative chemistry is subsequently accepted at 0.90x travel speed per actual pair, replacing its extra random slant. Special interactions remain pending.

goodChemistryProposal.recommendation: Retain existing 30% good-chemistry travel-speed boost per actual thrower-receiver pair. Apply separately on each relay leg and equally to compatible direct throws; no chain-wide bonus, no chemistry release shortening, no unlimited range.
goodChemistryProposal.scope: Good-chemistry trial treatment only. Negative chemistry/accuracy, special ability interactions, final long-range timing curve and range limits require separate review. For a fixed leg, target flight duration is otherwise-calibrated flight divided by 1.30; long-range penalties must not be removed or multiplied a second time as a separate chemistry reward.
goodChemistryProposal.referenceStatus: 1.30 is a verified current Harbor coefficient, not a verified universal Nintendo chemistry multiplier. Wii booklet confirms chemistry/buddy actions qualitatively. Newly indexed GC community mechanics excerpt is context-dependent and not treated as independently reproduced numeric evidence.

relayExample.status: Constant-speed counterfactual without long-range loss, equal arms and ready/aligned receivers. .20-second relay decision is unapproved. These examples isolate pair chemistry, not full candidate balance.

guardrails: Actual receiving player identifies the pair; affiliation with a third player does not boost the leg.
Do not compound two good relay legs into a 1.69x multiplier for the whole chain.
Preserve ordinary release visibility and real receiver coverage.
CPU forecasts use deterministic pair chemistry without rolling accuracy or consuming gameplay RNG; execution retains the same effective modifiers.
Trace pair identity and separate arm, chemistry and ability factors, plus each release/reception.
Neutral relay opportunities must still exist; chemistry enriches the choice rather than making it required for competent routine defense.
goodChemistryProposal.acceptanceEvidence: Jack replied approve to retaining the 30% good-chemistry speed boost per actual throw, with ordinary release unchanged.

formulas.commandToTarget: 0.30 + T (or Tgood); actual eligible reception may be later

longRangeProfileProposal.scope: Accepted original trial curve for ordinary throws; actual arm stat affects both base speed and comfortable range. Good chemistry applies once to full flight duration, not to range or release. Curve and first derivative are continuous at comfortable range. Direct throws remain available. Special abilities and negative chemistry are excluded from these original direct/relay comparisons; the accepted bad-pair treatment has separate examples below. Special interactions remain pending.
longRangeProfileProposal.basis: 160 ft is two C80 basepaths and below the old flat 200-ft CPU cutoff threshold. .60 s at 80 ft beyond range gives a small neutral relay advantage at an ideal 240-ft return after .30 s extra release plus illustrative .20 s extra decision. These are authored choices, not Mario measurements or sim results.

relayComparison.scope: Ideal collinear midpoint cutoff with receiver already ready; excludes pickup and ordinary pre-first-command thinking. Extra decision .20 s is illustrative, not an approved response or auto-relay delay.

alternatives.effect: Earlier long-throw loss and stronger relay incentive; weaker direct throws even from shallower positions.
Later long-throw loss and stronger direct throws; neutral relays become useful closer to the wall.

requiredChecks: Same physical model predicts and steps direct and relay trajectories; no outcome-only time addition.
Neutral, one-good-leg, both-good-leg and good-direct comparisons use actual paired characters and receiver coverage.
Include late/off-line cutoff and both input seats; do not infer automatic relay continuation from the illustrative .20 s gap.
Retain approved short infield timing, release and runner anchors; do not cap or hide an inconvenient direct outcome.
Replay fixed-input deep-gap/wall and full scoring cohorts, including unchanged mixed parks; deeper parks may expose over-penalized returns.
Trace total flight and long-range contribution; verify rendered arc/velocity realizes continuous timing without a midair pause.
Human standalone acceptance remains open; these calculations are not a tested game.
longRangeProfileProposal.acceptanceEvidence: Jack replied approve to the 160-foot ordinary-range profile and gradual slowdown for the first trial, including the presented arm and chemistry relationships.

negativeChemistryProposal.recommendation: Replace bad chemistry’s additional random slant branch with a predictable 10% travel-speed reduction for the actual bad thrower-receiver pair, applied once to full otherwise-calibrated flight. Preserve ordinary release; do not add a recovery pause or chemistry-only lateral miss.
negativeChemistryProposal.scope: Bad-pair chemistry only. This does not remove normal Field-dependent accuracy, bobbles, uncovered-receiver consequences, star effects or other errors; their calibration remains separate. Good and neutral pair anchors unchanged. Runtime and full scoring validation pending.

currentRule.probabilityScope: Assumes two executed independent bad-pair rolls; slant activation is not a guaranteed uncaught throw or out/safe verdict.

reference.scope: Nintendo explicitly describes bad chemistry sometimes producing off-target throws. The predictable penalty is an accepted deliberate Harbor deviation; 20%/0.70/10–14ft are audited Harbor values, not confirmed Wii parameters.

negativeChemistryProposal.tradeoff: Predictable lineup/routing cost supports attribution to player choices and more consistent routine races, at the cost of some Mario-like surprise/party volatility. Accepted reliable defense does not itself prohibit occasional bad-pair errors; Jack explicitly selected this deviation on September 14, 2026.
negativeChemistryProposal.alternative: Retain current occasional slower/off-target chemistry throws, then review probability and severity against ordinary defense. This keeps the reference-style surprise but permits a correctly commanded bad-pair throw to go astray.
requiredChecks: Apply only actual pair chemistry, once per leg; no chain-wide penalty.
Preserve 0.30-second ordinary release and real receiver coverage.
No guaranteed out or catch; ordinary accuracy and ball geometry remain authoritative.
CPU forecasts use the same deterministic pair factor without sampling future error RNG.
Version the changed random-draw schedule and replay baseline; removing a slant RNG branch changes later seeded outcomes even if unrelated rules are unchanged.
Re-run declared scoring cohorts and direct/relay traces rather than inferring balance from mean travel time.
Update governing chemistry spec and couch-facing explanation with implementation; do not silently remove legacy behavior in a research commit.
negativeChemistryProposal.acceptanceEvidence: Jack replied yes to the predictable 10% bad-chemistry speed penalty instead of its extra random misthrow chance.

relayOwnershipProposal.recommendation: Each human relay leg requires its own deliberate throw command. Permit an early command buffered for the next intended receiver; selecting a bag alone does not authorize throwing.
relayOwnershipProposal.currentBehavior: An explicitly armed ThrowBag is copied into _relayBag on a cutoff throw; after successful reception the human branch calls BeginThrowToBag automatically when _relayBag is valid. With no explicitly armed bag it holds. CPU re-evaluates its decision table.
interactionContract: The cutoff command authorizes the first leg only. A separate throw press authorizes the onward leg; merely holding the original button must not create another command.
Allow a deliberate early press for the intended incoming receiver so onward throwing need not require catch-frame timing. Numeric buffer window remains pending.
Without an onward command, the receiver holds the ball. Before the onward release motion begins, the player can cancel a queued command or change its target. Exact cancel mapping remains pending.
Start the ordinary 0.30-second release only after actual secure possession and any required recovery. No free release or artificial 0.20-second decision delay.
After release motion begins, the target is committed for that throw. No mid-flight retargeting.
Consume each queued command at most once, tied to the expected receiver and current play. Invalidate it on a missed reception, receiver change, play end or seat ownership change.
Use the same human ownership principle for cutoff returns and double-play throws, for either human defensive seat and both supported input schemes. CPU defense still selects its own throws.
relayOwnershipProposal.tradeoff: More control over holding and reacting to runners, plus one additional deliberate input per onward throw. Buffering reduces timing burden; automatic armed-route continuation needs fewer inputs but commits more of the play up front.
relayOwnershipProposal.referenceLimits: Wii printed page 10 and GameCube fielding controls document selecting a cutoff. Neither cited passage establishes the exact onward-command, buffering or cancellation behavior; this is an authored proposal, not a verified Mario control clone.
requiredChecks: Dead-stick armed cutoff holds after first leg
One deliberate second press produces one onward throw
Early/late command, hold, cancel and retarget boundaries
Missed catch and changed receiver cannot leak a queued throw
Both human defensive seats, both input schemes, CPU defense and double-play continuation
Full direct/relay race with actual per-leg release, movement and chemistry
relayOwnershipProposal.implementationBoundary: Accepted control direction only; reconcile §8.7 and the shared input contract in implementation, with docs/how-to-play.md and HowToPlay.cs updated together by the presentation owner. No runtime control change in this research commit.
relayOwnershipProposal.acceptanceEvidence: Jack replied approve to a separate command for each relay leg, with early-input buffering.

snapThrowProposal.recommendation: Replace the universal 1.22x flight-speed boost with a 0.22-second release after a cleanly received teammate throw. Retain 0.30 seconds for ordinary batted-ball catches, ground pickups and loose-ball recovery. Flight uses the ordinary arm, long-range and pair-chemistry rules.
snapThrowProposal.eligibility: The current uninterrupted possession began with a clean teammate-throw reception. A delayed command may use the benefit while that possession continues; dropping, bobbling or losing possession clears it. Required catch/tag/slide recovery is paid before release eligibility; no recovery bypass.

currentRule.scope: Applied to throws from the ability holder regardless of possession source, multiplying arm and pair chemistry.

snapThrowProposal.stacking: Chemistry modifies flight once, not release. Snap Throw does not boost range, accuracy or travel speed. Separate command per leg remains required; a buffered command starts release only after secure possession and required recovery.
snapThrowProposal.exampleScope: Analytical clean-reception command-to-target times. Field 5 rows isolate ability effect; Vale has Field 8. No simulation or guaranteed catch/out.
snapThrowProposal.tradeoff: A fixed 0.08-second release advantage gives a recognizable relay/double-play role while preserving readable flight. It is a substantial reduction of the old universal speed advantage, particularly on long throws and initial ground pickups; character balance needs review.
snapThrowProposal.alternative: Retain a universal flight-speed boost and calibrate its size; this preserves a broader arm advantage but overlaps the long-throw role.

references.scope: Nintendo names Quick Throw for Peach and Daisy; the cited roster text does not supply trigger/timing coefficients.
Original player guide by k_pflipsen describes quick fielding-to-throw action and relay/double-play usefulness; no measured 0.22-second value or definitive received-only trigger in that passage.

snapThrowProposal.referenceLimits: Mario-inspired role, authored scope and timing. The received-throw-only trigger is an explicit proposed Harbor rule here, not verified from the cited primary passages. No matched Wii/GameCube ability timing capture is available.
